channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: DP World denied security in fight over Djibouti port funds
item.description: A UK judge has rejected a demand by Dubai’s DP World for security for costs as it challenges a charging order made against funds linked to a container terminal in Djibouti that has spawned various arbitrations.

item.title: Panel rules in Bahamas port dispute
item.description: An UNCITRAL tribunal issued a partial award in a US$357 million dispute between the Bahamas and a privately owned port authority that operates a free trade zone – dismissing most of the government’s claims and all but one counterclaim.

item.title: Gazprom fails to unfreeze Wintershall assets
item.description: The Hague Court of Appeal has refused to lift an attachment over a Gazprom affiliate’s shares in a Wintershall joint venture, which were targeted by a Ukrainian energy company seeking to enforce a US$300 million investment treaty award against Russia.

item.title: Turkish contractor wins sunk costs in Ethiopia claim
item.description: A Permanent Court of Arbitration tribunal has rejected the bulk of a Turkish construction company’s treaty claim against Ethiopia, awarding it only sunk costs relating to an industrial zone development.

item.title: Sandoz loses ICC claim over drug impurities
item.description: A Chinese pharmaceutical company says it has defeated an ICC claim worth US$115 million brought by Swiss drugmaker Sandoz over alleged carcinogenic impurities in tablets for high blood pressure.

item.title: Eni and Nigeria settle billion-dollar corruption dispute
item.description: Italian energy company Eni says it will withdraw a billion-dollar ICSID claim against Nigeria after the parties settled their dispute over an oil prospecting licence that the state alleged was procured through corruption.

item.title: Simmons & Simmons hires from IBM in Tokyo
item.description: Chris Studebaker has left his role working in-house at IBM in Tokyo to join Simmons & Simmons as a disputes partner in the Japanese capital.

item.title: ICC panel narrows claims in Brazilian telecoms dispute
item.description: An ICC tribunal has struck out a significant number of claims brought by Brazil’s bankrupt telecoms operator Oi against a state agency in a multibillion-dollar dispute over an expired concession to provide landline phone services.

item.title: Darwazeh leaves Clyde & Co for Vanguard
item.description: Nadia Darwazeh has left her role as Paris head of arbitration at Clyde & Co to join the partnership at Vanguard International Dispute Resolution.

item.title: MOL enforces intra-EU ECT award in US
item.description: A US court has summarily enforced an Energy Charter Treaty award requiring Croatia to pay US$184 million plus interest to Hungarian oil and gas company MOL, rejecting the state’s arguments that payment would violate EU law.
